headlines.article_text: SAP weighs cutting at least 10,000 jobs in AI push: Bloomberg Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points SAP is weighing at least 10,000 job cuts as it reshapes its software business for the AI era, Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar with the matter. The number could change after labor negotiations. SAP did not immediately respond to a request for comment. SAP employs more than 110,000 people worldwide. In this article SAP Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT The headquarters of SAP AG, Germany's largest software company, on Jan. 8, 2013, in Walldorf, Germany. Thomas Lohnes | Getty Images News | Getty Images SAP is preparing a plan to eliminate at least 10,000 positions as the German firm reshapes its software business for the artificial intelligence era, Bloomberg reported on Thursday , citing people familiar with the matter. The number could change after labor negotiations. SAP did not immediately respond to a CNBC request for comment. Other software companies have also tied workforce reductions to AI initiatives, though for different reasons. WiseTech Global said in February it planned to cut about 2,000 jobs over two years as it integrated AI into its products and operations. Atlassian said in March it would cut about 1,600 jobs partly to fund further AI investment, while Cloudflare said in May it would eliminate more than 1,100 roles as it moved toward an AI-first operating model. In the U.S., employers cited AI in 121,401 job-cut announcements through October 2026, accounting for about 20% of the total, according to a Nov. 5 report from outplacement and executive coaching firm Challenger, Gray & Christmas. SAP employs more than 110,000 people worldwide. Bloomberg reported that all departments had been asked to identify potential cuts, with product, engineering and sales in particular focus. The company also underwent a reorganization in 2024, when it eliminated around 10,000 positions through a program that relied mainly on voluntary departures and retraining. Its headcount later remained relatively flat as it hired for new roles, Bloomberg reported. In 2023, SAP CEO Christian Klein told CNBC he did not necessarily expect a reduction in the workforce, saying he expected the company to grow and "accelerate" its total revenue. watch now VIDEO 6:50 06:50 SAP CEO Christian Klein says there are more A.I. use cases coming down the pipeline Closing Bell: Overtime The reported cuts come as Klein pushes SAP toward an AI-first strategy . This year, SAP completed four acquisitions — Reltio, Dremio, Prior Labs and TechWolf — and made strategic investments in AI-focused companies including Parloa, n8n and Conduct. The acquisitions are intended to help SAP organize company data, develop AI models for business information and analyze workforce skills.
